the-playbook-asks-for-five-things-before.text: The playbook asks for five things before anyone draws: what the icon is (app, favicon, tray), a one-word essence, the brand color, a personality lane, and where the icon will live small. The distilled rule from the casebook is blunt: <0>choose the user’s job, not the category noun</0>. “Route”, “decide”, “compare” and “scout” produce better marks than “game”, “conference” or “travel”, because category nouns are where clichés live.

distinctiveness-in-this-system-means-spe.text: Distinctiveness in this system means specificity. The strongest marks in the casebook <0>are</0> a specific, ownable thing — a price tag, a cut gem, a folded route map, a maneki-neko — whose blacked-out silhouette names an object rather than a category. A bare initial on a gradient tile is named in the docs as the single most common way an AI icon looks competent and forgettable at once.

for-privacy-sensitive-products-the-brief.text: For privacy-sensitive products the brief is reduced to a neutral job verb, and the public case record keeps the visual evidence without the category noun, repository names or local paths.

for-one-brief-the-designer-human-or-agen.text: For one brief the designer (human or agent) sketches at least four concepts through different lenses — the literal object, a metaphor, the core verb, a letterform <0>fused</0> into the object, an abstract system, or a negative-space dual reading. Two concepts that share a silhouette count as one.

a-documented-clich-table-pairs-each-prod.text: A documented cliché table pairs each product category with its overused symbols and a direction to push toward instead. The rule is simple: if your concept is the “avoid” cell, it is not done. The house list also refuses to represent “AI” with brains, robots, sparkles, wands, neural nodes, or the default blue-to-purple gradient.

one-device-a-dual-reading-ownable-geomet.text: One device — a dual reading, ownable geometry, a fused letterform, an unexpected crop, an ownable color pairing, or a single accent. Then four hard tests before any polish: the <0>name-the-thing test</0> at 128px and at 16px (a passing answer is a concrete noun), the <1>silhouette test</1> with color removed, the <2>maskable test</2> (essential detail inside the central 40%-radius safe circle), and the <3>row test</3> against eight competitor favicons. Finalists are then baked off side by side with <4/>, and the winner is judged by shape, not by 128px color.

every-master-is-drawn-at-0-at-16-pixels-.text: Every master is drawn at <0/>. At 16 pixels, 64 grid units are roughly one output pixel, so the budget is explicit: every idea-carrying accent gets about two pixels (≈128 units), every required separation at least one, and strokes thinner than about 2.3% of the side are expected to vanish. Essential content stays in the central ~80% safe area; anything that must survive an adaptive crop stays inside the central safe circle. A 16px icon has room for exactly one idea, and two opaque foreground elements must never cross.

The 20-study Social Signals set assigns styles with a seeded <0/> checked against the catalog before any render, and keeps each study’s path geometry inside its build script. The 400-cell Emoji Matrix is built by <1/>, which re-runs <2/> on every cell, fingerprints every proof, and fails closed if one receipt, digest or review decision is missing. Scale buys repeatability and auditability — never a pass.

the-renderer-treats-svg-as-untrusted-inp.text: The renderer treats SVG as untrusted input. Chromium runs with network and service workers blocked, page JavaScript disabled, active or animated content removed or frozen, and sRGB, locale and timezone fixed. Input is capped at 4 MiB, 50,000 elements and 128 nesting levels, and DTD or entity declarations are rejected. The 16px and 128px PNGs on this page are those exact renders, not resamples of a larger image.

For the 400-cell matrix a similarity report adds exact PNG hashes plus 64-bit alpha and luminance difference hashes; pairs whose combined alpha-plus-luminance Hamming distance is within 12 (same meaning) or 6 (different meaning) are flagged high risk, and exact duplicates block integration. The script calls the distance “a triage signal for visual inspection, not an admission score”.

the-reviewer-opens-the-contact-sheet-and.text: The reviewer opens the contact sheet and Review Lab: rows on white, dark and mid-gray; columns from 16px to 256px at actual size; a pixel-zoom strip; alpha footprint; visual silhouette; adaptive-crop previews; every selected target transform. Six axes are scored 1–5: legibility at 16px, distinctiveness, balance and grid, color and contrast, scalability, craft. Nothing ships below 4 on any axis, and distinctiveness is an explicit gate — a generic silhouette scores at most 3 no matter how nice the color is.

if-an-axis-is-under-4-the-reviewer-names.text: If an axis is under 4, the reviewer names the weakest axis, makes the single highest-impact change, and re-renders. The docs expect two or three passes. The 100-case gallery edition admitted 100 of 111 candidates and explicitly rejected eleven weaker, less legible or repetitive directions; Keepsake Knot’s receipt records that its first pass was rejected for reading as a power symbol.

the-exported-receipt-carries-a-0-of-the-.text: The exported receipt carries a <0/> of the exact SVG and a <1/> binding the project, target set, colors, Electron radius, color scheme, tray mode and tray-source hash. <2/> verifies both, requires an empty warnings list, <3/> and six scores of at least 4, then re-runs automated QA before writing a single file. Change the SVG’s content — the digest ignores only line endings — and the receipt is stale.

every-shipped-icon-ends-with-0-first-pas.text: Every shipped icon ends with <0/>: first-pass and final scores, the cliché avoided, the signature device, one reusable lesson. <1/> surfaces the weakest recurring axis and house clichés; the lessons are distilled into numbered rules in <2/> (54 at the time of writing) that the next brief must read first. An unrecorded icon teaches the system nothing.

The code is Apache-2.0; the IconFlow name and mark are subject to the project’s <1>trademark policy</1>. Documents: <2>SOCIAL_SIGNALS.md</2>, <3>EMOJI_MATRIX.md</3>, <4>GALLERY.md</4>.
